title: Rav Chaviva of Mechoza
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman says that he always discusses matters with Rav Ashi as a student-colleague, as in Shabbat 87b, Eruvin 57a and Bava Kamma 72a. In Bava Kamma there, when he raised a difficulty against Rav Ashi, “Rav Huna son of Rava said to him”; Hyman says that it should read Rav Acha son of Rava.

notes.text: The William Davidson digital Bava Kamma 72a spells Chavivi of Mechoza and has Rav Huna son of Rava answering the objection; Hyman’s Chaviva form and proposed Acha emendation remain explicit. His “always” and student-colleague characterization are preserved as his assertions.
The consulted Bava Kamma paragraphs give Chavivi and Huna. Hyman says the latter name should read Acha. His description of Chaviva’s relationship to Ashi is an attributed judgment.
